findings.summary: Teardown needs a consumer-withdrawal barrier before checking that mounts are gone.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/67/design.md:113-117 checks for live consumer pods/mounts and then removes TLS/proxies/server, but never withdraws the still-bound consumer claim or prevents new use of it. Under spec.md Tenant/S4, an ordinary unprivileged pod creator in the authorized consumer namespace can create another allowed PVC-using Pod after that check; Restricted admission explicitly allows persistentVolumeClaim volumes (Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/). Its kubelet mount can race proxy unmount/removal or a later reuse of the per-export port. UID ownership checks protect which objects are deleted but do not serialize this new mount against down, so S7 teardown cannot prove consumers have stopped.
findings.fix: Define a minimal durable withdrawal/quiescence protocol before the no-consumer check, for example remove the exact owned consumer-claim UID from usable service and wait for claim protection plus existing and in-flight node mounts to retire, or use an equally concrete admission barrier. Keep the barrier effective across interruption/resume and refuse proxy/port/server retirement while any old consumer operation remains ambiguous. Reuse of names/ports must not authorize an old mount against a replacement export. Add fake/API/node fixtures creating a new Pod and delaying a mount between the initial check and removal, plus interrupted/resumed withdrawal and claim/port replacement. Preserve backing data and the existing no-force-unmount rule.

findings.summary: The new tenant-driven server and tunnel processes lack a finite resource-containment profile and pressure qualification.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/67/design.md:94-101 qualifies capabilities/seccomp but specifies no CPU/memory/pid/fd or connection/handshake/buffering limits for Ganesha, its pod tunnel or the host node proxies. Contracts at :121-127 and tests at :142-148 likewise omit pressure/exhaustion behavior. Authorized unprivileged consumers can generate many opens/locks and concurrent filesystem operations; a network peer reaching the TLS listener can also occupy pre-authentication work. Neither root squash nor mTLS bounds that work. Ganesha documents independent RPC_Max_Connections, RPC_Ioq_ThrdMax, DRC and send/receive-buffer controls (https://github.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/blob/next/src/doc/man/ganesha-core-config.rst), but this plan does not select/qualify even an overall containment boundary. An unconstrained gateway or host proxy can exhaust resources shared with the storage node, beyond the export trust boundary.
findings.fix: Add a bounded per-export qualification profile using ordinary container/service CPU, memory, task/fd controls and supported server/tunnel connection, handshake and buffer limits, with explicit overload/timeout/restart semantics preserving stable-write and recovery rules. Exact version-specific values may remain in the approved qualification artifact, but finite budget categories, host-proxy containment and pass criteria must be required now. Add future slow/failed TLS handshake and concurrent NFS open/request pressure fixtures proving bounded ownership/cleanup and safe recovery after containment kills. This does not require filesystem quotas, a custom transport-memory proof or a new replication protocol.

report: Full independent security review of all #67 intent/spec/design/decisions/local ADR at exact HEAD, preserving the Nov13 accepted first-step Ganesha VFS, NFSv4.1, node-local mTLS tunnel and qualification approach. Checked tenant/claim/namespace/PV trust boundaries, current Persistent-only Flaminio CSIDriver and CSI mount lifecycle, lab bootstrap/RBAC, node-pinned restart and process exclusion, private recovery state, TLS identity/expiry/rotation and teardown ownership. Read relevant current #79 mount-ownership and #82 failover invariants at recorded hashes without reopening them. Primary Kubernetes Pod Security/Admission and ephemeral-volume documentation confirms Restricted allows PVC/CSI/ephemeral volumes; no speculative inline-CSI bypass finding is asserted because current lab driver is Persistent-only and the plan separately requires alternate helper denial. Primary Ganesha VFS/core docs support the privilege and resource-control analysis; version/privilege qualification deferral itself is not a defect. Two Medium findings above; no additional Nits. No node-loss/RWX provisioning/per-user authentication/quotas or simulator expansion invented. No runtime, server/client, prototype, implementation tests, lab, benchmark, disk, tracker or child-agent action; future qualification tests remain proposed. Static diff whitespace and final issue/dependency HEAD checks passed; checkout remained exact and clean. Only this JSON report was written. External sources reviewed: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/ ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/ ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/ephemeral-volumes/ ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ ; https://github.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/wiki/VFS ; https://github.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/blob/next/src/doc/man/ganesha-core-config.rst .
